reading.body:
Google's Franklin County facility is part of a multi-county Columbus-area data center campus that has received $1.7 billion in announced investment alongside new facilities from AWS and Meta in the same corridor. The operator does not publish power capacity, square footage, or exact site boundaries at the individual building level, disclosing only aggregate figures by state on its data center location pages. This disclosure policy means the facility's actual IT load capacity cannot be determined from public sources.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities but only 8 with published power specifications in this registry, totaling 60.4 MW. This Franklin County facility ranks ninth among Ohio sites by published megawatts, though its actual capacity remains undisclosed and may be substantially larger than the state ranking suggests. The published figure for this facility is therefore not available.

The scale of Google's investment in the New Albany and Columbus corridor indicates material hyperscale infrastructure buildout in central Ohio, but without published power capacity for individual buildings, the Franklin County site's contribution to state and national AI compute availability cannot be quantified from operator disclosures alone. Regional grid constraints and interconnection costs for the multi-county campus would require state Public Utilities Commission filings or utility-side data to assess.
